transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. I understand the operations team has proposed an automated warehouse project with a $10 million vendor quote to improve order throughput at our main distribution center. The vendor is offering either an outright equipment purchase or a five-year lease. As the decision-maker on this capital allocation, I'd like to follow our normal review process. Before I settle this proposal, I'd like to hear from accounting control and tax on any issues they see with either option. Let's start the roundtable — who has something to raise?

transcript.text: Elena, before we proceed, I need to flag an important accounting issue I discovered this week while reviewing the vendor's invoice coding. Of the $10 million total quote, $2.4 million is actually implementation consulting and configuration support — not equipment. Under our capitalization policy, that portion must be charged to operating expense. That leaves exactly $7.6 million eligible for capitalization. I have not yet posted this correction to the project file, but it will materially affect the capital budget for this proposal regardless of whether we go with the purchase or the lease.

transcript.text: Elena, I have a tax issue to raise. I received a tax memo this morning confirming that the qualifying automation equipment can receive the accelerated-depreciation election only if the company purchases and owns it rather than leases it. This memo has not yet been circulated to the capital-review file, so I'm surfacing it now. This is a material consideration for the purchase-versus-lease decision: if we lease the equipment, we would forgo the accelerated depreciation benefit that would be available if we purchase and own it outright.
